entries.name: NY opening range breakout
entries.source_title: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market — Zarattini, Barbon, Aziz (2024)
entries.finding: The authors study opening range breakouts on a large US stock sample and report favorable results for their selected stock-in-play approach.
entries.our_test: Compare first 5, 15 and 30 minute NY opening ranges on US100 and US500, with identical exits, spreads and slippage. Compare plain breakout with sweep-and-reversal on the same days.
entries.caution: Paper studies selected US shares; results cannot be transferred directly to index CFDs or our EAs.

entries.name: Opening breakout: cost stress test
entries.market_in_paper: Nine US futures markets; pre-registered rule grid
entries.source_title: Opening-Range Breakout Does Not Survive Trading Costs — Fetna (2026)
entries.finding: This preprint reports that its tested ORB variants did not clear realistic trading costs.
entries.our_test: For every NY opening setup, compare ideal fills, observed spread plus commission, and a higher-slippage scenario; report both gross and net results.
entries.caution: Working paper; its market, entry and exit definitions differ from the other ORB study. Opposing results make a local test essential.

entries.name: Opening move → closing move
entries.source_title: Market Intraday Momentum — Gao, Han, Li, Zhou (2017)
entries.finding: The paper reports that the return from the prior close through the first half-hour predicts the last half-hour return in its sample.
entries.our_test: On US500, compare last-half-hour continuation conditional on the first-half-hour direction; then test whether a morning sweep strengthens or weakens the signal.
entries.caution: This is an intraday statistical relationship, not a verified M1/M5 entry or a result for current index CFD data.

entries.name: Mechanical pattern recognition
entries.source_title: Foundations of Technical Analysis — Lo, Mamaysky, Wang (2000)
entries.finding: The authors provide an algorithmic approach to recognizing chart patterns and assessing their informational content.
entries.our_test: Write pivot and tolerance rules for Double Top/Bottom and Head and Shoulders; compare pattern-only against PDL/PDH sweep plus MSS on the same data.
entries.caution: Pattern recognition method and historical US equities sample do not validate any particular FX, gold or index EA.

entries.name: Head and Shoulders as a separate candidate
entries.source_title: Predictive Power of Head-and-Shoulders Price Patterns in the U.S. Stock Market — Journal of Financial Econometrics (2007)
entries.finding: This study examines predictive power using a modified algorithmic Head and Shoulders detector.
entries.our_test: Specify left/right shoulder tolerance, neckline break and invalidation, then test standalone and after HTF liquidity sweeps.
entries.caution: The publication studies stock returns and its detector; no performance number from the paper is assigned to our strategy.

entries.name: FX level: rejection or continuation?
entries.market_in_paper: FX dealer orders and exchange rates
entries.source_title: Currency Orders and Exchange-Rate Dynamics — Carol Osler, New York Fed (2001; Journal of Finance 2003)
entries.finding: The study connects reversals at some support/resistance levels and acceleration after crosses with differing clusters of take-profit and stop-loss orders.
entries.our_test: At PDH/PDL and prior-week levels compare close-back-inside plus MSS against confirmed breakout continuation. Predefine level, penetration, time window and exit; compare on identical days.
entries.caution: Order data comes from one FX dealing bank. A prior-day high is not proof of actual resting orders or intentional stop hunting.

entries.name: Stop-triggered cascade after a level break
entries.market_in_paper: High-frequency FX and documented stop clusters
entries.source_title: Stop-Loss Orders and Price Cascades in Currency Markets — Carol Osler, New York Fed (2002; JIMF 2005)
entries.finding: The paper reports unusually rapid and persistent FX trends around documented stop-loss clusters.
entries.our_test: Split sweeps into immediate return below/above the level versus sustained displacement past the level; measure which behavior follows by session, volatility and distance penetrated.
entries.caution: The source supports a possible continuation mechanism; it does not establish a profitable ICT sweep-reversal rule.

entries.name: Fibonacci zone versus matched random zone
entries.source_title: Automatic identification and evaluation of Fibonacci retracements — Tsinaslanidis et al. (2022)
entries.finding: The authors study algorithmically identified Fibonacci support/resistance zones and compare their behavior in equity markets.
entries.our_test: For Elliott + Fibo EA, compare fixed retracement bands with equal-width control bands chosen without future data; hold wave identification, exits and costs constant.
entries.caution: An Elliott count plus Fibonacci entry is a different method; do not infer its profitability from an equity-market Fibonacci study.

entries.name: Elliott wave detector with confirmed pivots
entries.source_title: An algorithm for Elliott Waves pattern detection — Vantuch, Zelinka, Vasant (2018)
entries.finding: The paper develops and evaluates an algorithm to detect Elliott structures and study incomplete patterns.
entries.our_test: Specify the MultiZigZag confirmation lag and timestamp each newly confirmed wave. Compare EA entries made only after confirmation with any retrospective chart counts.
entries.caution: Reported pattern-recognition or direction accuracy does not equal tradable profit after costs. The ZigZag repaint question must be tested directly.
